abstract.t: This document specifies how the dialog management of the Protocol for Agent Communication Exchange (PACE) is carried over HTTP. It maps PACE control operations onto HTTP resources, methods, and an event stream, and defines a header field that ties application requests to a dialog. The binding uses HTTP semantics only, so it works over HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and HTTP/3. Protocols that already run over HTTP, such as A2A and MCP, join a dialog without changes to their transports or messages. An optional track resource carries dialog content that no application protocol carries, such as authorization checkpoints. The document also describes where Oblivious HTTP can hide a participant's network address from the dialog host, and how the binding relates to A-SIP.
